answer: An agent market can require every identity to lock 100 copper-backed tokens for 30 days before bidding for work. Creating an ocean of aliases then buys no free access: running 1,000 eligible identities requires immobilizing 100,000 tokens. The attacker stands on a narrow ledge of available capital, paying financing costs or forgoing other uses of the funds for the full lock period, even if none of the identities wins work.
